newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai Lujiazui sees 1996 net flat.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai Lujiazui sees 1996 net flat.

text.p: Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development sees 1996 net profits flat but earnings per share down sharply due to its large scale rights and bonus issue, officials and analysts said on Monday.
A company official said it expected 1996 net profits of 590 million yuan, slightly up from the 585 million yuan in 1995.
He said that profits mainly came from the first half of 1996 because the company completed no big property deals in the second half of the year.
The company posted net profits of 548 million yuan in the first six months of 1996, up from 266 million yuan in the same 1995 period.
An analyst with a foreign investment company said Lujiazui's earnings per share would fall sharply because of its rights issue and bonus issue in the second half of 1996.
He expected the company to post earnings per share of about 0.44 yuan in 1996, down from 0.80 yuan in 1995.

The company's current total share capital rose to 1.334 billion shares, up from 733 million shares at the end of 1995, after a three-for-10 rights issue at a price of 5.50 yuan in November and a four-for-10 bonus issue in December.

The company's B share closed at $0.840 on Monday, down from $1.00 on December 31, on expectations of poor results and profit-taking following the listing of its four-for-10 bonus issue today, brokers said.
A local broker said profit-taking in Lujiazui was likely to continue with many investors selling shares they obtained at a price of about $0.4-0.5 thanks to the rights and bonus issues.
